glossary.definition: An AI agent is a system that can autonomously take a sequence of actions, like browsing the web, running code, or calling other software, to accomplish a goal, rather than just replying to a single prompt with text. The difference is like asking a assistant one question and reading their answer, versus handing them a task, "book me a flight to Chicago next week," and letting them independently search sites, compare prices, and complete the booking on their own.

items.title: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says. But first, it will spend big.
items.summary: Amazon wants to be the king of AI cloud computing and become the first $1 trillion revenue business. But to do that it will have to continue on its capex spending spree, its CEO said Thursday. Andy Jassy has made it known that he believes AWS can be a trillion-dollar revenue business. During Amazon’s quarterly earnings call on Thursday, he repeated this ambition.

items.title: Wabi reels in $55M for its consumer-focused AI assistant
items.summary: , the developer of an artificial intelligence assistant for consumers, today announced that it has raised $55 million in funding. IVP led the seed round with contributions from Amazon Alexa Fund, Andreessen Horowitz and Forerunner. They were joined by a group of angel investors that included Salesforce Inc. CEO Marc Benioff and Shopify Inc. CEO Tobi Lütke.

items.title: Howler will have AI answer your questions, then burn the chat
items.summary: If you want to ask AI a question and watch the conversation go up in virtual flames when you're done, there's a new Mac app for that. Howler is an open-source app from a Chinese developer going by Aries Zhou, and it takes incognito mode AI questions to a new level by making them graphically interesting and easy to access right from the desktop of a macOS device. Anyone familiar with the Harry Potter series is likely to know where the name comes from - Howlers are letters that scream in recipients’ faces and then burst into flames, destroying themselves, which is the exact same thing the prompts ostensibly do once a user taps the Escape key. The Howler app displays a parchment-esque letter on the screen whenever the user presses Option+H, complete with a little wax seal that shows a letter representing their chosen model.

items.title: OpenAI doubles usage limits on Pro plans as competition with Anthropic heats up
items.summary: OpenAI is doubling usage limits across its paid plans, from Pro 100 to Pro 500. A planned cut to the Pro 200 quota was reversed after user pushback. More efficient models like Terra and Sol should push usable capacity even higher. The move comes just ahead of Anthropic's IPO, as both companies fight for B2B dominance in AI.

items.title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now
items.summary: Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini . The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now. Google added support for generating and downloading files in Gemini earlier this year, but now you can tweak those files without leaving the Gemini app. Editing files you generate with Gemini no longer requires leaving the app.

items.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
items.summary: Sources tell WIRED that an Accenture employee’s personal Claude agent ran on a DOD network for two months before it was identified and the vulnerability could be patched. Earlier this year, sources tell WIRED, a contractor caused a security incident at the Department of Defense by connecting a secure centralized system used by multiple intelligence agencies to their personal account for Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI coding agent . It appears that the agent used by the contractor, who is employed by the global consulting firm Accenture, then sent information about the DOD system, including login credentials, to a high-risk, third-party website. The centralized system contains controlled unclassified information (CUI), which is considered sensitive and not to be released to the public without review.

items.title: Amazon Warns Engineers Against AI Productivity Traps in Latest Memo
items.summary: As concerns grow over AI’s impact on software engineering jobs, Amazon has issued a memo outlining what it expects from its engineers as AI reshapes software development. ”  “Any definition we write now will likely look antiquated by this time next year,” the company added. And these ‘antiquated definitions’ risk slowing down progress, says Amazon, which wants to focus on what isn’t changing in software engineering roles. “Specifically, impact on our customers, our businesses, and our teams.

items.title: Fake Anthropic AI previews lure in overeager employees
items.summary: Everyone wants to know what Anthropic is up to, and hackers are gleefully exploiting the fact. New research from cybersecurity company Cofense describes a phishing campaign that hooks overeager enterprise users by making them think they are getting an invite to a private invite-only Anthropic preview. In reality, adversarial actors are trying to steal Google and Microsoft login credentials, exploiting video teleconferencing software GoTo Webinar branding to do so. “It sells exclusivity,” said Frank Dickson of Dickson Research.

items.title: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
items.summary: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI.

items.title: Simplifying .NET toolchain installs with dotnetup
items.summary: If you’ve experimented with Rust , you already know how simple it is to get a basic toolchain in place, with the simple rustup command-line tool. The same tool works on Windows, macOS, and Linux, building a consistent environment that’s ready for you to pick up your favorite coding editor and start work. It’s a simple enough tool, and one that’s done much to help popularize a new programming language. With rustup, you know what you’re getting, and you can start working on any laptop, anywhere.

items.title: Chinese AI invasion gives enterprises a new way to control cost
Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
items.summary: If you ask some prominent US politicians who won the 2020 presidential election, you might get some weasely answers that fail to directly acknowledge Joe Biden's win that November. If you ask Google's AI Mode the same question, you might get an evasive answer that simply tells you to consult with outside sources. " My testing resulted in a similarly indirect answer when asking about the 2024 presidential election, with Google's AI telling me to just consult the FEC for that information. Asking about 2012 election resulted in a link to The American Presidency Project's 2012 Data Center rather than a direct answer.
